title: Lieb-Robinson bounds for irreversible dynamics via adaptive Dyson expansion
authors: Carla Rubiliani, Marius Wesle, Tom Wessel
abstract: In this note, we study a broad class of time-dependent and irreversible dynamics for quantum spin systems in both finite and infinite volume. We develop a simple and flexible strategy for expanding commutators of the form $[A,τ_{s,t} \, B]$ in terms of self-avoiding paths of sets, where $A$ and $B$ are local operators and $τ_{s,t}$ is the Heisenberg time evolution. This adaptive Dyson expansion requires no backwards time evolution and is thus also applicable to irreversible dynamics. Furthermore, we discuss how such an expansion directly implies Lieb-Robinson bounds. A central feature of our result is that the obtained Lieb-Robinson bounds are independent of any Hamiltonian and dissipative on-site terms of the generator.
summary: This paper introduces an adaptive Dyson expansion technique to analyze time evolution in quantum spin systems undergoing irreversible dynamics. By expanding commutators using self-avoiding paths, the authors derive Lieb-Robinson bounds that are remarkably general, holding true regardless of the specific Hamiltonian or dissipative terms used to generate the evolution.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive Lieb-Robinson bounds for the dynamics of quantum spin systems, specifically extending these bounds to cover irreversible dynamics.
main_result: A novel adaptive Dyson expansion is developed that yields Lieb-Robinson bounds independent of the specific Hamiltonian or dissipative on-site terms generating the dynamics.
method: The core method involves constructing an adaptive Dyson expansion for commutators using sums over self-avoiding paths of sets, which then directly implies the locality bounds.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum spin systems evolving under time-dependent and irreversible dynamics, modeled by local, time-dependent dissipative terms (Lindbladian dynamics is a special case).
key_observables: Lieb-Robinson bounds, which quantify the finite speed of propagation of quantum correlations, and the norm of the commutator $\left\|[A, 	au_{s,t} B]ight\|$.
important_parameters: The time separation ($t-s$), the distance between local regions ($d(X,Y)$), and the structure of the dissipative generator $\Phi$.
main_assumptions: The dynamics are generated by local, time-dependent dissipative terms, and the method relies on the algebraic framework of a quasi-local algebra.
paper_structure: The paper follows a two-step structure: first, deriving the adaptive Dyson expansion for the commutator, and second, using this expansion to derive the Lieb-Robinson bounds.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general mathematical tool to prove locality bounds for open quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding thermalization and correlation spreading in many-body physics.
